Background

PSAT/SAT Test Administration
• Since 2017 the Rhode Island Department of Education has
administered the PSAT as part of the spring test administration
to 10th graders
• Since 2018 the Rhode Island Department of Education has
administered the SAT to 11th graders.
• Both the PSAT and SAT include sections in ELA and
Mathematics.

Transition to Digital SAT
• In 2024, the College Board transitioned to the Digital SAT
administration platform.
• Several aspects of the assessment changed during this transition in
terms of both user facing features (computer versus P&P
administration) as well as backend features (adaptive versus fixed-
form).
• Changes in the results in 2024 from 2023 led to concern amongst
some states about test equivalence.
• The analyses in this presentation are intended to support discussions
about the equivalence of tests and comparability of results.
Summary PSAT/SAT Data

Introduction
• We examine student performance on the PSAT/SAT in several ways
• Participation frequencies
• Mean/Standard Deviations of Scores by year
• Mean/Median Baseline SGP by year (SAT only)
• Baseline SGPs are normed using pre-pandemic, PSAT-SAT growth
norms.

2023-2024 from prior years.
• Both ELA and Mathematics SAT saw decreases in mean scaled score,
particularly in 2023-2024. Mathematics dropped from 461.5 to 445.9.

Baseline SGPs
• Because growth conditions on prior scores, baseline SGPs are much more
robust to changes in the population of students tested than status
measures.
• Baseline SGPs were fairly stable across the last several years in ELA, less so
in mathematics. The drop in the mean SGP to 44.4 in 2023-2024 in
mathematics is synonymous with the drop in achievement observed.
• The low median SGP in mathematics was caused (largely) by low SGPs of
students in the 6th, 7th, and 8th prior score deciles.

Conclusions
• Results comparing 2023-2024 SAT results with prior years indicates
discrepancies in mathematics which suggest assessment changes may have
• In general, assessment changes are always accompanied by score
discrepancies such as those observed here.
• Drawing firm causal conclusions isn’t substantiated with these secondary
analyses. However, further investigations into digital SAT test format —
particularly for higher achieving students where lower growth was observed
— may lead to causal factors leading to lower scores.
